tasks.name: Finalize Developer task contract
tasks.description: Complete the ticket-selection, implementation, testing, UI-validation, failure, evidence, branch, skill, and checkpoint rules for one engineering ticket per turn.
acceptance_criteria: The engineering plan remains authoritative while a fingerprinted compact index handles selection.
The implementation, verification, blocker, result, branch/worktree, and checkpoint rules are explicit.
The contract is adapted to the approved Bun, Vite, Tailwind, TypeScript, Supabase, and DigitalOcean stack.
UI rules identify exact approved mockup, interaction, copy, token, font, logo, icon, and brand sources.
Every referenced skill has an exact verified ID and installed path or a verified installation source.
tasks.verification: deterministic/manual contract review: source paths resolve, skill registry resolves, ticket-index commands pass, and a selected ticket can be extracted without loading the full plan
tasks.notes: Reconciled from the legacy scaffold draft and completed during turn 6.

tasks.name: Finalize product QA contract
tasks.description: Define integrated user-story, recovery, accessibility, security, browser, real-device, and defect-triage verification after engineering completion.
acceptance_criteria: The QA inventory source and one-case-per-turn selection rules are explicit.
Severity, evidence, retest, and release-blocker rules are explicit.
QA binds to one frozen candidate and cannot be silently replaced by dev auto-deployment.
Customer journeys use the in-app Browser and add physical-device evidence for hardware/realtime behavior.
Failure, accessibility, responsive, auth, isolation, privacy, and provider-boundary coverage are explicit.
Failed cases route through Developer repair and deterministic retesting.
tasks.verification: manual contract review: QA source, candidate, evidence, failure, defect, and release-gate rules are complete and mutually consistent
tasks.notes: Reconciled from the legacy scaffold draft and completed during turn 6.

tasks.name: Finalize release and deployment contract
tasks.description: Define production-readiness review, DigitalOcean deployment, migration, secrets, smoke, monitoring, rollback, evidence, and release-completion rules.
acceptance_criteria: The QA-to-release gate and recorded medium-exception path are explicit.
Development and production use separate DigitalOcean apps, Supabase environments, secrets, domains, data, and triggers.
Developer mutates only development; DevOps promotes only the exact QA-approved immutable images to production.
App-spec, migration, secret, domain/TLS, health, worker, logs, alerts, smoke, monitoring, and rollback checks are explicit.
Production completion requires zero test data and a complete release record.
tasks.verification: manual contract review: development/production boundaries, release queue, production mutation, rollback, and completion evidence resolve without conflict
tasks.notes: Reconciled from the legacy scaffold draft and completed during turn 6.

tasks.name: Validate and activate the engineering delivery loop
tasks.description: Complete the source map, status mapping, branch contract, skill registry, compact work selection, sanity check, and queue binding.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh agent can locate the next eligible work item without chat history or loading the full engineering plan.
All source paths, stage gates, verification rules, status mappings, and state transitions resolve without contradiction.
Development/production deployment and Supabase boundaries agree across architecture, plan, and workflow.
The approved plan is bound as authority and the workflow is active without a separate activation approval.
The six loop sanity questions have concrete answers in the package.
tasks.verification: deterministic/manual review: validate JSON, resolve source and skill paths, check the ticket index, run the six-question sanity check, and confirm loop_status is active
tasks.notes: Completed during turn 6 after reconciling legacy progress/task drift. No legacy placeholder timestamp is treated as wall-clock audit evidence.
